scenario.name: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide, Microsoft & MITRE — Cluster-Wide Malicious DaemonSet Scheduling & Node RootFS Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a sunlit city park with green lawns, shade trees, winding stone footpaths, wooden benches, and a tiered stone water fountain at the center. Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches. A watchful park ranger at the corner kiosk notices the exact same bench receiving repeated timed drop-offs and logs the suspicious pattern on the patrol board. In this scenario (T1610, NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide, Microsoft & MITRE, Cluster-Wide Malicious DaemonSet Scheduling & Node RootFS Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: creating an apps/v1 DaemonSet with Wildcard, then daemonSet Controller Scheduling Pods, then control-Plane Static Pod Manifest Inspection. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Creating an apps/v1 DaemonSet with Wildcard, then DaemonSet Controller Scheduling Pods, then Control-Plane Static Pod Manifest Inspection, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 201 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Creating an apps/v1 DaemonSet with Wildcard Tolerations (operator: Exists)
stages.subtitle: Execution & Persistence (T1610 - Deploy Container)
stages.description: Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the park ranger go about their routine. The actor submits POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/daemonsets containing spec.template.spec.tolerations: [{operator: "Exists"}] so the DaemonSet bypasses node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule taints (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with ResourceType=apps/v1 DaemonSet , kube-system/node-log-sync, TaintToleration=tolerations: [{operator: "Exists"}] , Includes Control-Plane Nodes, CreatorIdentity=system:serviceaccount:monitoring:prom-operator so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get daemonsets --all-namespaces -o wide (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get daemonsets --all-namespaces -o wide configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1610 during "Creating an apps/v1 DaemonSet with Wildcard Tolerations , operator: Exists" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '. | select(.objectRef.resource=="daemonsets" and .verb=="create")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.objectRef.resource=="daemonsets" and .verb=="create"' /var/log/kubernetes/a so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1610 during "Creating an apps/v1 DaemonSet with Wildcard Tolerations , operator: Exists" , The actor submits POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/daemonsets containing spec.template.spec.tolerations: [{operator: "Exists"}] so the DaemonSet bypasses node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule taints while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/daemonsets (name=node-log-sync) / ⇠#1 ACK 201) from Node ① (#1 Compromised Namespace ServiceAccount) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 All Cluster Worker & Control-Plane Nodes).

keySpecs.value: Remove daemonsets create/update permissions from workload ServiceAccounts and enforce Kyverno/OPA policies blocking wildcard NoSchedule tolerations outside approved system controllers.

stages.title: Stage 2: DaemonSet Controller Scheduling Pods with hostNetwork, hostPID & hostPath Across All Nodes
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1610 - Deploy Container)
stages.description: Minutes later, an accomplice walks past the central park fountain, retrieves the hidden slip from the bench without speaking a word, and drops a replacement set of instructions. Here in Step 2 inside the city park, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the city park later without disturbing the quiet botanical greenhouse. The DaemonSet controller reconciles the new specification and spawns node-log-sync-<hash> pods on every node in the cluster with hostNetwork: true, hostPID: true, and a hostPath volume mounting /var/log and /etc (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with ControllerActor=system:serviceaccount:kube-system:daemon-set-controller, ScheduledNode=control-plane-01, PodSecuritySpec=hostPID=true, hostNetwork=true, hostPath=/etc so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=node-log-sync -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,HOSTNET:.spec.hostNetwork (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=node-log-sync -o custom-columns=NAME:.metad so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1610 during "DaemonSet Controller Scheduling Pods with hostNetwork, hostPID & hostPath Across All Nodes" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl describe daemonset node-log-sync -n kube-system runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl describe daemonset node-log-sync -n kube-system configuring pod security c so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1610 during "DaemonSet Controller Scheduling Pods with hostNetwork, hostPID & hostPath Across All Nodes" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ DaemonSet controller creating pod kube-system/node-log-sync-x9k2p on control-plane-01 / ⇠#2 ACK 201) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver (/apis/apps/v1/daemonsets)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 All Cluster Worker & Control-Plane Nodes).

keySpecs.value: Enforce Kubernetes Pod Security Admission (PSA) Restricted or Baseline labels on namespaces to reject pods requesting hostNetwork, hostPID, or hostPath volumes.

stages.title: Stage 3: Control-Plane Static Pod Manifest (/etc/kubernetes/manifests) Inspection & DaemonSet Purge
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Hidden in plain sight among joggers and park visitors, the pair moves confidential slips across the open park lawn without ever stepping near the guarded city hall across the street. In this final step inside the city park, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches until the park kiosk patrol log catches the mismatch. Running on the control-plane node with /etc mounted, the DaemonSet pod inspects /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ and /etc/kubernetes/pki/. Defenders delete the DaemonSet and audit static pod manifests for unauthorized modifications (logged in Linux Audit Event 257 with AccessedControlPlanePath=/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml, SourcePod=kube-system/node-log-sync-x9k2p, FalcoRule=Read Sensitive File Untrusted so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl delete daemonset node-log-sync -n kube-system (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl delete daemonset node-log-sync -n kube-system configuring pod security con so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1611 during "Control-Plane Static Pod Manifest , /etc/kubernetes/manifests Inspection & DaemonSet Purge" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact sha256sum /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , sha256sum /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Control-Plane Static Pod Manifest , /etc/kubernetes/manifests Inspection & DaemonSet Purge" , Running on the control-plane node with /etc mounted, the DaemonSet pod inspects /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ and /etc/kubernetes/pki/ while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Reading /host/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml from DaemonSet container / ⇠#3 ACK 257) from Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver (/apis/apps/v1/daemonsets)) to Node ④ (#4 kube-scheduler & DaemonSet Controller), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 All Cluster Worker & Control-Plane Nodes).

keySpecs.value: Monitor /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ and /etc/kubernetes/pki/ with host FIM (auditd / Falco) and prevent workload ServiceAccounts from deploying into kube-system.
